curriculum.title: Cambridge Lower Secondary Science
curriculum.note: The Cambridge Lower Secondary Science framework is not in this class folder on Google Drive, which holds only scanned resource packs with no text layer, so this map works at strand level. The strands, the sub-strands named under each, and the five types of scientific enquiry on the Home tab are the published Cambridge ones; only the individual objective numbers are missing. This map follows the 2020 series, the direct continuation of the Primary 0097 framework used lower down this school. If the school teaches the older 1113 framework instead, the same content is organised as Scientific enquiry, Biology, Chemistry and Physics, without a separate Earth and Space strand. Add the Stage 9 framework and the exact codes can be attached lesson by lesson.

objectives.title: Thinking and Working Scientifically. Sub-strands: models and representations; scientific enquiry: purpose and planning; carrying out; and analysis, evaluation and conclusions
Biology. Sub-strands: structure and function; life processes; ecosystems
Chemistry. Sub-strands: materials and their structure; properties of materials; changes to materials
Physics. Sub-strands: forces and energy; light and sound; electricity and magnetism
Earth and Space. Sub-strands: planet Earth; Earth in space; cycles on Earth
Science in Context, connecting science to the learners' own lives, their school, their island and the wider world

ongoing.title: The five types of scientific enquiry
ongoing.blurb: Cambridge asks that learners meet all five, not only fair testing. At lower secondary they also plan more of the enquiry themselves. Each practical below is one of the five; check across a term that all five have been used.

items.title: Finding information from books, the internet and video, and judging its reliability
Changing one variable, controlling the rest, and measuring the effect
Taking measurements or observations across minutes, days or a season
Sorting and grouping by observable and measurable properties, and using keys
Looking for patterns and relationships in data that cannot be fully controlled
